phase3_findings.description: lib/test/run.sh:25252 — the assertion `#1618/#1897 skill-body: that reason no longer names the SKILL.md file path` pipes `sbl_run ... 2>/dev/null` into `grep -q ... && echo no || echo yes`, and its expected value is `yes`. `yes` is produced by grep's FAILURE arm, so a helper crash (traceback, argparse change, unreadable fixture, python3 resolution failure) yields empty stdout, greps as a plain miss, and the assertion passes GREEN while measuring nothing — and the `2>/dev/null` removes the one channel that would have made the crash visible. This is the only sbl_run call site in the file that discards stderr while consuming stdout (line 25445's `>/dev/null 2>&1` is a legitimate exit-status test), and its sibling one line above at 25250 correctly omits the redirect. It also contradicts the contract comment `sbl_run` itself adds in this same diff: 'Do not discard stderr in a caller either: callers capture stdout alone, so a helper traceback would vanish and a crash would read as a plain grep miss.' Remedy: drop the `2>/dev/null` and make the pass value a positive observation (e.g. extract the rendered directory operand and assert it equals `skills/review`), so the assertion goes RED both on a regression to the file path and on a helper that produces no output at all.

phase3_findings.description: docs/internal/skill-body-load-delivery.md still carries two sentences describing the verdict as derived from the Skill tool_result: line 468 ('deriving a per-root verdict from the Skill `tool_result` in the execution file through scripts/skill-body-load-probe-verdict.py') and lines 490-492 ('the verdict is derived from the Skill `tool_result` recorded in the execution file — the rendered body itself — checked against controls read from disk'). The same page's own session-C section later states the opposite ('the tool_result is a launch stub ... and the rendered body arrives in the next record'). Graded Suggestion, not a carve-out: neither line is diff-added or diff-modified (so Phase 4.1.6's promote-only sweep does not reach them), both sit inside session B's explicitly frozen and 'Superseded in part' record, which this repository's past-time-snapshot convention says not to rewrite, and both are documentation prose rather than a comment or an assertion message — the population AC9 names. If left as-is, consider one pointer sentence at the top of the session-B block naming the operand correction, rather than editing the frozen text.

The `_pairs_for_root` docstring in scripts/skill-body-load-probe-verdict.py carries roughly seven lines of derivation and provenance beyond its specification statement (why collect_skill_pairs serialises the whole input, what 'a dated observation of one runner version' means, how the divergence would be unfalsifiable from inside the suite). It is a function docstring, not a module docstring or contract header, so the prevention-only comment standard's specification carve-out does not cover it. The clause worth keeping inline is the prohibition plus its one consequence: do not narrow this to a named field — a field-keyed read would answer `unestablished` on every real transcript while every fixture stayed green. The rest already has a home in docs/internal/skill-body-load-delivery.md.

The AC8 're-derivable from repository bytes alone' promise has no driving assertion. The two committed-transcript assertions drive `recorded Skill tool_use pairs: 1` and the controls arm being reached via a deliberately absent --root; neither asserts a `delivered-whole` verdict against the real transcript's bytes. Both docs/internal/skill-body-load-delivery.md and the fixture header state the cell is now re-derivable — true today, verified by execution, but nothing in the suite keeps it true, so it can silently become a documented falsehood. The ingredients are already present: extract `git show 668a7899...:skills/review/SKILL.md` into a `$SBL_TMP/rederive/skills/review/` layout and assert `sbl_run "$SBL_OBS" --tier review --root prflow:review=skills/review/SKILL.md | grep -c 'VERDICT: delivered-whole'` equals 1. This is the one assertion that would exercise the whole binding -> directory-selection -> controls -> verdict chain on production bytes rather than on the instrument's own assumptions — the very rationale the fixture header gives for committing it.

The new load-count operand in the never-loaded reason is undriven. `verdict_for_root` renders '... %d Skill load(s) were recorded in total' % (skill_name, len(pairs)); swapping `len(pairs)` for `len(matches)` — provably 0 on that arm — leaves every assertion green, because the only test touching the arm (`sbl_says null_input 'no recorded Skill tool_use names prflow:review'`) greps the prefix and stops before the count. The `null_input` fixture records exactly one pair, so extending that grep to '1 Skill load(s) were recorded in total' pins it at no extra cost. Alternatively drop the operand: `audit()` already prints `recorded Skill tool_use pairs: N` on its own line.

The one-control fixture's tail control is degenerate. `printf 'a
b
c
'` gives tail == 'c', a single character present in essentially any delivered body — including the `Base directory for this skill: ...` prefix line — so the `tail not in body` branch cannot fire for this fixture and its positive control (delivered-whole count 1) proves less than it appears. Not a false green: the assertion it guards (the mid-is-None wording) does discriminate. A distinctive short tail such as `zzq` would make the control mean what it claims.

The no-following-body reason asserts a load of the root 'was recorded' in exactly the disclosed residue case where none was. For `arg_equals_other_root` — a `prflow:implement` load whose serialised input carries `"prflow:review"` as an argument — `_pairs_for_root` binds it, the directory selection then refuses it, and the printed reason reads 'the Skill load of prflow:review was recorded but no following body record naming its own directory ('skills/review') was found'. No Skill load of prflow:review was recorded. The verdict (`unestablished`) is correctly fail-closed and the arm is deliberately pinned, but the reason is the sentence a maintainer transcribes into the durable record, so a false 'was recorded' clause is the same silently-wrong-testimony class this PR exists to close. A phrasing naming what was actually matched (e.g. 'a recorded Skill load naming %s in its input') keeps the arm and the pinned substring `no following body record naming its own` intact.
